title: TanStack Router: typed routes, search state and loaders
objectives: Build a typed route tree — file-based (`createFileRoute` plus a generated tree) or code-based (`createRoute`, `getParentRoute`, `addChildren`) — and register the router so `Link` and `navigate` are type-checked
Write a `validateSearch` that turns untrusted URL search params into typed state with fallbacks, and update search with an updater that keeps the other params

Load a route's data before render: `loaderDeps` for the search values the loader uses, and a loader that fills the query cache (`queryClient.query({ …, staleTime: 'static' })`, formerly `ensureQueryData`) for `useSuspenseQuery` to read
Predict what the user sees on a navigation: when the loader re-runs, when the pending component appears, and what a missing `loaderDeps` does

questions.prompt: What does `declare module '@tanstack/react-router' { interface Register { router: typeof router } }` buy you?

options.text: `Link`, `useNavigate` and `redirect` are type-checked against your route tree
It registers the routes at runtime, so `RouterProvider` can match URLs against them
It's what makes file-based routing generate `routeTree.gen.ts`
It injects the router into every loader's `context`

questions.explanation: A `declare module` block is erased at compile time: it's declaration merging, pure TypeScript. It tells the library's top-level exports which router your app uses, so `<Link to="/post">` is a compile error with a "did you mean '/posts'" hint. The runtime router comes from `createRouter` and `RouterProvider`; the generated tree comes from the bundler plugin or CLI; loader context comes from `createRootRouteWithContext` and `createRouter({ context })`.

questions.prompt: In code-based routing, why does every non-root `createRoute` need `getParentRoute: () => parentRoute`?

options.text: Both: the router builds the route's full path from it, and the types inherit through it
Only for TypeScript: at runtime the tree comes entirely from `addChildren`, so it's erased
It sets the order in which sibling routes are tried when matching a URL
It lets the parent route be code-split and loaded only when a child matches

questions.explanation: The docs justify it with type safety — a child route inherits its parents' params, search and context through it — but it's also used at runtime: in Router 1.170 a route's id and full path are built from its parent's, and a child route without it fails an invariant when the router builds the tree. Matching order and code splitting are unrelated.

questions.prompt: `?page=2` arrives in `validateSearch` as the number `2`. Why validate at all?

options.text: The URL is user input: `?page=abc` and `?page=-3` arrive too
Because the router hands every search value over as a string, and validation converts it
Because routes without `validateSearch` ignore the query string
Only so TypeScript knows the type; at runtime the return value is discarded

questions.explanation: The router JSON-parses first-level values, so numbers and booleans keep their types — but `abc` is still `"abc"` and nothing stops `-3`. `validateSearch` is the trust boundary: its return value is what `useSearch`, `loaderDeps` and the loader receive, so returning fallbacks there keeps every consumer simple. Without it the raw values still reach `useSearch` — just untyped and unchecked.

questions.prompt: On `/posts?page=1&tag=react`, the Next link is `<Link from="/posts" search={{ page: page + 1 }}>`. Where does it go?

options.text: `/posts?page=2` — the object replaces the whole search, dropping `tag`
`/posts?page=2&tag=react` — the router merges an object into the current search
It doesn't compile: the search object is missing the `tag` key
It throws at runtime, because the new search no longer matches the route's schema

questions.explanation: An object is the new search, full stop. The updater form, `search={(prev) => ({ ...prev, page: prev.page + 1 })}`, keeps everything else. Optional keys make the bug invisible to TypeScript. (Run headlessly: the object link's `href` was `/posts?page=2` and the updater's kept every other param.)

questions.prompt: A `/posts` loader reads `page` from `location.search` and has no `loaderDeps`. The user clicks from page 1 to page 2. What happens?

options.text: The loader doesn't re-run; the component suspends on page 2 and the pending component flashes
The loader re-runs, because the URL changed and loaders run on every navigation
Page 1 stays on screen for good, because the loader never runs again for this route
The router throws an error: loaders may only read search params through `loaderDeps`

questions.explanation: Loader results are keyed by pathname plus `loaderDeps`. Without deps, `?page=2` is the same key, and in a headless run the loader didn't run again. The page still ends up right — the component asks for page 2 and `useSuspenseQuery` fetches it — but by suspending, so the user sees a loading flash and the waterfall the loader was meant to prevent. `loaderDeps: ({ search }) => ({ page: search.page })` fixes it.

questions.prompt: Which loader body matches what `ensureQueryData` did, in TanStack Query v5.102+?

options.text: `context.queryClient.query({ ...postsQuery(deps), staleTime: 'static' })`
`context.queryClient.query(postsQuery(deps))`
`context.queryClient.prefetchQuery(postsQuery(deps))`
`void context.queryClient.query({ ...postsQuery(deps), staleTime: 'static' })` — without returning it

questions.explanation: `ensureQueryData` meant "cached data if there is any, otherwise fetch". With `staleTime: 'static'`, `query` treats any cached data as fresh, which is the same thing — the migration guide's own replacement. Plain `query` uses `staleTime: 0`, so it refetches even when cached (headlessly: two calls for two loads, versus one). `prefetchQuery` is deprecated too and swallows errors. Not returning the promise means the router doesn't wait — fine for streaming non-critical data, wrong for what the page needs to render.

questions.prompt: With default router options and `loaderDeps` in place, the user clicks **Next** and page 2's loader takes 3 seconds. What do they see?

options.text: Page 1 for about a second, then the `pendingComponent` until page 2 is ready
The `pendingComponent` immediately, for 3 seconds
Page 1 for 3 seconds, then page 2 — the pending component only shows on first load
A blank outlet until page 2 is ready

questions.explanation: The router waits for the loader and keeps the current page rendered meanwhile. Only past `pendingMs` (default 1 s) does it show the route's `pendingComponent`, and then for at least `pendingMinMs` (default 500 ms) so it doesn't flash. An immediate pending component is the symptom of a component that suspended — usually missing `loaderDeps`.

prompts.prompt: Declare a code-based child route and build the tree.
prompts.explanation: `getParentRoute` links the child to its parent (for the full path and for inherited types); `addChildren` assembles the tree that `createRouter({ routeTree })` matches against. File-based routing generates both for you in `routeTree.gen.ts`.

prompts.prompt: Validate the search: a page that isn't a positive integer falls back to 1.
prompts.explanation: `Number(...)` turns `2`, `"2"`, `"abc"` and `undefined` into `2`, `2`, `NaN` and `NaN`; `Number.isInteger` rejects `NaN` and `1.5`. Whatever the URL held, the route sees a valid number.

prompts.prompt: Make the loader depend on `page` only, and fill the query cache before render.
prompts.explanation: `loaderDeps` declares what the loader reads, so changing `page` re-runs it and other params don't; the loader receives the result as `deps`. `staleTime: 'static'` makes `query` return cached data when there is some — the replacement for the deprecated `ensureQueryData`.

prompts.prompt: Go to the next page and keep every other search param.
prompts.explanation: The function form receives the current search; spreading it keeps `tag`, `sort` and anything else. An object literal would replace the search entirely.

snippets.question: What's logged?
snippets.explanation: The router JSON-parses each first-level value: `2` and `true` become a number and a boolean, while `react` isn't valid JSON and stays a string. So does `007` — JSON has no leading zeros — which saves an id like `007` from becoming `7`. Validation still has to handle each case. (Logged headlessly with Router 1.170.)

code: // On page 1, the user clicks Next. Page 2 takes 2 seconds to load.
snippets.question: How many times does the loader run for page 2, and what is on screen during those 2 seconds?
snippets.answer: Zero times; "Loading posts…" shows at once, until page 2 arrives
acceptable: the loader doesn't re-run; the pending component shows immediately
snippets.explanation: Without `loaderDeps`, a search-only change keeps the same loader key, so the router doesn't re-run it. The component then reads page 2, which isn't cached, and `useSuspenseQuery` suspends — the route's pending component shows immediately instead of page 1 staying up. With `loaderDeps`, the loader fetches page 2 while page 1 stays on screen. (Both behaviours observed headlessly with Router 1.170.)

snippets.question: What `href` does each link render?
snippets.explanation: An object *is* the next search; a function receives the current one. Link A silently drops `tag` and `sort`; link B keeps them. Both type-check if those keys are optional in the route's search type. (The rendered `href`s were checked headlessly.)
